note: Owner-scoped tables not cleared by one or both deletion cascades. Worked through with the developer on 2026-09-04, 9 entries -> 2: MemoryVersion, EcoAuth, OwnerAgentDefault, AgentUsageEvent, AgentUsageDaily, AgentUsageEventArchive and GroupShare joined BOTH cascades, and each is now asserted row-by-row in test/unit/storage-conformance.test.ts rather than only named here. A deleted username is released for reuse (decision 2026-08-10), so anything left in this file is inheritable by the next registrant and needs a reason that survives being read aloud to the person whose account was deleted.

exempt.AppPurchase: REVIEWED 2026-09-04, and it must outlive its owner. Developer's decision, in his words: it is accounting, and the law requires it to be kept. A purchase has two sides, and the row is simultaneously the buyer's receipt and the seller's book entry, so deleting it with the buyer would remove a record the seller is required to hold and did not consent to lose. This is the same answer the finance tables get, and for the same reason the check's own header already gives for keeping them out of OWNER_COLUMNS. Retention and erasure were reconciled on 2026-09-24 (audit A8-4): the row is kept, but the erased person's side of it is pseudonymised in both deletion cascades. When the buyer's account is deleted, buyerGaii and buyerOwner become one random `erased:` token per erasure, which no account can ever be named and nobody can compute from the name; the seller's side gets the same when the seller's account is deleted. The node's signature over the old identity is cleared with it, because it would confirm a guessed name. The amounts, the dates, the app and the other party stay for the books. Before this, the kept row still named its parties by `name@node`, the coordinate every purchase read keys on, so whoever registered a freed name next received the receipts, the paid content and a valid licence.
exempt.AiProvenance: REVIEWED, and it must outlive its owner. Exposed 2026-08-29 when `principal` was added to OWNER_COLUMNS — the addition that also revealed Connection, which was fixed rather than exempted. A provenance record answers "which model made these exact bytes, and how much was a person involved?" for content that can outlive the account: a published app, a public memory, anything another node fetched. GET /v1/provenance/by-hash is the EU AI Act detection access point and is deliberately unauthenticated for public content, so deleting the record with the account would break the answer for content still readable, which is the opposite of what the marking is for. The personal data in the row is the principal string, and it is the point of the record rather than an incidental field. If a person's account goes and their content stays public, the honest fix is to take the content down with it, not to strip the label off it. Retention and erasure were reconciled on 2026-09-26 (secaudit 2026-09, A8-4), the way AppPurchase was: the row is kept, and both deletion cascades rewrite its ownerGhii and principal columns to the erasure's random `erased:` token, which no account can ever be named. Those two columns are the node's own lookup data beside the statement, and every owner read keys on ownerGhii: the owner's list, the owner view, the owner's hash lookup and attaching a record to new content. Before this, whoever registered a freed name next read the previous person's records as their own. The statement document, generator included, stays as it was.
